title: Marketing Creative Agency Scope Tasks: What Vendors Clean Room by Room
seoTitle: Marketing Creative Agency Scope Tasks: Room-by-Room Checklist
metaDescription: Marketing creative agency scope tasks by room, with minutes per visit and which items raise labor 10–25%. Use the checklist, then price it in our calculator.
excerpt: An agency cleaning scope has to handle café-style kitchens, content studios, and lounge furniture that standard office checklists skip. This room-by-room guide lists daily, weekly, and monthly tasks and shows which ones add billable labor.
quickAnswer: A creative agency scope should cover nightly kitchen and coffee bar sanitation, restrooms, trash, and vacuuming, plus weekly upholstery and glass work and monthly high dusting and studio care. Kitchens, lounge soft seating, and photo or podcast studios push labor 10–25 percent above a standard office of the same size. At national rates, a 3,500 sq ft agency prices at $0.09–$0.15 per sq ft per visit plus $15–$30 per restroom and $12–$25 for the kitchen.

blocks.text: Start With Rooms, Not a Generic Checklist

Most janitorial proposals include a boilerplate checklist written for a carpeted suite with cubicles. Agencies rarely look like that. A typical creative office mixes an open studio floor, glass-walled meeting rooms, a reception lounge designed to impress clients, a kitchen that doubles as an event space, and often a photo, video, or podcast room. Each needs different tasks, tools, and time.

The fastest way to get accurate bids is to send a room list with square footage and the tasks you expect in each. Vendors then price real work instead of padding for unknowns, and you have a document to inspect against.

blocks.caption: Daily agency scope with typical minutes per visit (3,500 sq ft example)
rows: Trash and recycling, vacuum or dust mop, wipe cleared desks, push in chairs
Fluff and crumb-vacuum sofas, wipe tables, dust mop entry hardwood, spot-clean glass doors
Wipe tables, clean whiteboards if cleared, reset chairs, vacuum
Interior glass add-on $15 – $35 weekly or per visit
Kitchen and coffee bar (250 sq ft)
Degrease counters, sink, appliance exteriors, empty organics and recycling, mop floor
Disinfect fixtures, restock, mop, polish mirrors
Empty trash, dry vacuum floor and seamless area, never touch gear

blocks.text: Totaled, that is roughly 1.8 to 2.6 labor hours per visit for a 3,500 sq ft agency. A carpeted office of the same size at about 3,500 sq ft per labor hour plus two restrooms would need roughly 1.4 to 1.7 hours. The difference comes mostly from the kitchen, lounge furniture, and glass.

items: Weekly: vacuum upholstery on lounge sofas and booth seating with an upholstery tool, lifting cushions.
Weekly: clean all interior glass partitions and doors with streak-free method; agencies with glass-heavy layouts often move this to every visit.
Weekly: wipe chair arms, bases, and monitor arms with damp microfiber.
Weekly: descale and wipe kitchen sink fixtures and clean the microwave interior.
Monthly: high dust ductwork, exposed beams, and pendant lights in loft ceilings using a HEPA vacuum with extension.
Monthly: wipe baseboards, door frames, and switch plates throughout.
Monthly: clean refrigerator interior on a scheduled day after staff purge notice.
Quarterly: hot-water extraction of carpet zones or scrub and recoat of hard floors at $0.03 – $0.06 per sq ft per month amortized.

blocks.title: Wet Floors in Hardwood Lofts
blocks.text: Damp mopping kitchens and restrooms in an open loft creates slip risk for staff working late. Require crews to place four-sided caution signage, such as a 36 inch Rubbermaid wet floor cone with bilingual English and Spanish print, at every wet zone, and use low-moisture methods on hardwood. OSHA walking-working surface rules make slip prevention a shared concern for the vendor and tenant.
Which Specialty Tasks Raise Labor Above Standard Rates

Four agency features consistently raise labor. Café-grade kitchens with espresso machines and heavy daily use require degreasing and floor mopping every visit. Lounge upholstery, velvet and boucle especially, needs tool changes and slower passes. Glass partitions, which define most modern agency layouts, add streak-free detailing that can consume 15 to 30 minutes per visit. Content studios slow crews down because cyc walls, lighting stands, and seamless backdrops must be avoided.

Event aftermath is a fifth category that should never be absorbed into the base contract. Post-event cleanups usually bill at the specialty hourly band of $55 – $95 because they involve bulk trash, sticky floors, and late hours. Ask for a pre-priced event clean so account teams can pass the cost through to client budgets.
Air, Cloths, and Signage Standards to Write In

Open lofts with exposed ceilings and limited return air can feel stuffy after events. The Alen BreatheSmart 75i covers roughly 1,300 sq ft with medical-grade HEPA, a laser particle sensor, and a quiet run mode suited to meeting areas. Decide whether filter replacement is a tenant or vendor duty and write it into the scope.

Specify a color-coded microfiber program. Rubbermaid HYGEN 16 by 16 inch split-microfiber cloths are bleach safe and rated for about 500 commercial launderings, and assigning separate colors to restrooms, kitchen, and glass prevents cross-contamination from toilet fixtures to coffee bars, a common inspection failure.

items.name: List every room with square footage
items.text: Include studios, phone booths, lounges, and storage so vendors price real conditions.

items.name: Mark restricted zones
items.text: Content studios, server closets, and prop rooms get dry-only or no-entry status.

items.name: Assign frequencies
items.text: Use daily, weekly, monthly, and quarterly columns, aligning kitchen intensity with headcount.

items.name: Request minutes per room
items.text: Have bidders show time by room so you can compare with the 1.8 – 2.6 hour benchmark above.

items.name: Inspect monthly
items.text: Score each room against the scope and tie repeated failures to credits in the contract.

faqs.q: How many labor hours should a 3,500 sq ft agency need per visit?
faqs.a: With a working kitchen, lounge furniture, glass meeting rooms, and two restrooms, plan on about 1.8 to 2.6 labor hours per visit. A plain carpeted office of the same size would need about 1.4 to 1.7. Bids far outside that range should come with a room-by-room time breakdown.

faqs.q: Who handles Safety Data Sheets for cleaning chemicals in our office?
faqs.a: Under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard, the cleaning contractor must keep Safety Data Sheets and proper labels for every product it brings on site, and train its workers. Agencies should ask for the vendor's chemical list and SDS access, especially if the kitchen or studio uses products such as stainless polish or gaffer-tape adhesive removers.

faqs.q: Does our cleaning vendor need bloodborne pathogen training?
faqs.a: Yes, for restroom cleaning and any spill response involving blood or bodily fluids, OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires the employer to provide training, PPE, an exposure control plan, and hepatitis B vaccine availability. Confirm it in writing and keep a bodily fluid spill kit on site.

faqs.q: How do weekly and monthly tasks show up on the invoice?
faqs.a: Most vendors fold weekly and monthly tasks into a flat monthly fee calculated on 4.333 weeks per month. Quarterly floor care is usually amortized monthly or billed when performed. Ask for both approaches in the bid so you can choose predictable billing or pay-as-performed.

faqs.q: Should our agency use a day porter instead of more night visits?
faqs.a: A day porter makes sense when the kitchen and restrooms get heavy use, or when clients visit daily. Porters are billed hourly, typically $35 to $65, and two to three hours a day can let you cut night visits from five to three while keeping client-facing areas sharp.
